content.text:
**Finding submitted: compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment. Stopping tool calls here.

The repair this round was to resolve, rather than merely assert, the recurring failed check. A full-text search establishes that the check is unsatisfiable on this document by any verbatim quote:

- `"for convenience"` → one hit only, in §22 captions boilerplate (p0088, "included for convenience of reference only") — unrelated to termination.
- `"may terminate"` / `"without cause"` → **no hits**.
- Termination-election language → p0079 only.

So there is no express "Client may terminate for convenience" grant anywhere to cite. The right exists but is drafted obliquely, as TrueLink's obligation to keep serving until the Client-elected termination date. I quoted the full §14 sentence as the primary evidence and documented the search result so the miss is traceable to phrasing rather than to a gap in the bargain.

Substance, per the verifier's own analysis and unchanged across submissions:

| Element | Position |
|---|---|
| Client at-will exit, ~30–60 days' notice, no exit fee | Preferred |
| No TrueLink mid-term convenience exit (§§2–3 cut-off is cause-based) | Preferred |
| 12-month term | Neither walk-away trigger engaged |

Two shortfalls remain noted rather than flagged: no express pro-rata refund (moot under §5a's monthly arrears billing) and the mutual 30-day non-renewal notice, which benefits us equally.

One genuine item I could not close from the reviewed text: §14 is "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 4 was not supplied. §6 (p0047) suggests it covers minimum monthly fees. If Section 4 preserves those fees post-termination or otherwise conditions Client's right, it would function as a de facto early-termination charge and this rule should be reopened — worth requesting Section 4 before the finding is relied on as final.
